faq.q: When does the 2026–27 wedding season start?
faq.a: The first vivah muhurat after Dev Uthani Ekadashi (20–21 November) is Saturday 21 November 2026, followed by 24, 25 and 26 November and 2–6, 11 and 12 December. There are no muhurat dates from 16 December to 14/15 January (Kharmas). Dates restart on 15 January, February has 13 dates, and the last dates before mid-April are 1–4, 9, 10 and 14 March, per the New Delhi panchang. Confirm local dates with your pandit.

faq.q: Which month has the most wedding dates in 2026–27?
faq.a: February 2027, with 13 muhurat dates (2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14, 15, 21, 22, 25, 26, 27 and 28), as listed by most panchangs. Plan stock, staff and offers for it during the December–January break.

faq.q: When should a shop start wedding season marketing?
faq.a: Three to four weeks before the first dates. For the 21 November start, update your Google Business Profile and WhatsApp catalogue in the last week of October, start reels and a dated Google offer in early November, and follow up with reviews and broadcasts in mid-November.

faq.q: Can I send wedding offers on WhatsApp to all my customers?
faq.a: WhatsApp Business broadcast lists only reach contacts who have saved your number, up to 256 per list. Send one useful message with the dates and how to book, rather than many reminders. Larger campaigns need paid tools, and customers should have agreed to hear from you.

faq.q: Do I need to label a paid collaboration with an influencer?
faq.a: Yes. ASCI’s guidelines require a clear label such as "Ad" or "Collaboration" that is upfront and hard to miss, not hidden among hashtags. In videos, the label should appear on screen. This applies to free gifts too, not only paid posts.

posts.seo_title: Why Google Reviews Disappear (2026): 9 Reasons | U Scale
posts.seo_description: Google reviews disappearing from your business? The 9 reasons it happens, what changed in 2026, who can appeal, and how to protect your reviews.

faq.q: Why did my Google reviews suddenly disappear?
faq.a: The most common reason is Google’s spam filters, which remove reviews that break its policy and sometimes remove genuine ones by mistake. Other reasons include a sudden burst of reviews, reviews collected with discounts or staff targets, a customer editing or deleting their review, the reviewer’s account being restricted, a profile merge or reinstatement, a review pause on your profile, or a Google-side issue.

faq.q: Can I get deleted Google reviews back?
faq.a: Google says reviews removed for policy violations won’t be restored. If a genuine review was removed, the customer who wrote it can appeal once from their own Google Maps profile, and Google restores it if it was removed in error. As the owner, you can contact Business Profile support.

faq.q: How long does a Google review appeal take?
faq.a: Google says evaluating a reported review typically takes several days, and it gives no fixed time for appeals. In October 2026 a Google staff member reportedly said appeals were delayed by high volume. Send one complete request and don’t file duplicates.

faq.q: Why is a customer’s Google review not showing?
faq.a: Google checks reviews before publishing them, which can take a few days. Older phones or app versions can cause problems, and filtered reviews may appear in the customer’s own profile marked "Not posted". Ask them to check Your contributions in the Maps app.

faq.q: Can Google stop my business from getting new reviews?
faq.a: Yes. If Google finds fake reviews, it can pause new reviews for a set period, unpublish existing reviews, or show customers a warning that fake reviews were removed. It emails the owner, and you can appeal through Google’s form.

content.text: Yesterday your shop had 128 Google reviews. This morning it shows 97. Nobody told you anything, and the reviews that vanished were from real customers. It's one of the most stressful things a local business owner can see, and this year it has been happening a lot.
Google
says

it blocked or removed over 292 million policy-violating reviews in 2025. Most of those were fake. Some were not. This guide explains every reason reviews disappear, how to tell which one hit you, what changed in 2026, and the appeals you can actually make. Spoiler: owners can appeal less than most blogs claim.
The short version:

first check while signed in to Google on the Maps app, because signed-out views can show fewer reviews. If one review is gone, the reviewer probably edited or deleted it, or Google filtered it, and only the reviewer can appeal that. If many vanished at once, check your email for a Google notice about a pause or restriction, and wait a few days before you act. Send one support request, not ten. Then make your review flow steady and policy-safe, so it doesn't happen again.
First, check that they're really gone
Before you panic, do these four checks. They take two minutes.
Sign in, and use the Maps app.
Since 30 September, Google Maps has been
reported
to ask signed-out visitors to sign in to read more reviews. Google hasn't announced this. If you checked from a signed-out browser, you may simply be seeing fewer.
Check from your owner view.
Open
business.google.com
and select Read reviews. That's the full list Google is showing for your profile.
Think about recent profile changes.
If your profile was merged with a duplicate, Google
says
reviews from both "might take a few days" to display.
Ask one affected customer to look.
In the Maps app, under Your contributions and then Reviews, a removed review may still show with a label such as "Not posted". If they see it there, it was filtered, not deleted by them.
9 reasons Google reviews disappear
1. Google's spam filters removed them
This is the most common reason. Google's own help page

faq.q: How much does a website cost in Mumbai in 2026?

faq.a: Website design is taxed at 18% GST when the designer is GST-registered. Freelancers only have to register once their turnover crosses ₹20 lakh a year, and an unregistered freelancer can’t charge GST. Always ask whether a quote includes GST.

faq.a: Yes. Register the domain in your business’s name with your own email, and keep the registrar login, the hosting login and the website admin login. Without them you can’t move or fix your site if the designer disappears.

faq.q: Why is one website ₹10,000 and another ₹1 lakh?
faq.a: Cheaper sites are usually a ready-made theme with your logo and photos added. Higher prices pay for custom design, written content, features such as booking or payments, more products, SEO groundwork and support after launch. Ask what’s included before comparing prices.

content.text: Ask three Mumbai web designers what a website costs and you can get three answers that are ten times apart. Price guides published by Mumbai agencies this year put a basic business website anywhere from ₹8,000 to ₹50,000, and a custom one at up to ₹2 lakh. Both ends can be honest. They are just not the same product.

I build websites for shops, clinics and small businesses in Mumbai, and I publish my prices. This guide covers what a website really costs in Mumbai in 2026: the going rates, what you get at each level, the bills that arrive every year after launch, GST, and the questions that protect you before you pay anyone, including me.
The short version:

a basic 3–5 page business website in Mumbai costs about ₹15,000–₹50,000 from most designers, a custom-designed one ₹40,000–₹2 lakh, and an online store ₹25,000–₹3 lakh depending on products and features. After the first-year offers end, budget about ₹4,400–₹9,400 a year (before GST) for the domain and hosting. Registered agencies add 18% GST. Whoever builds your site, the domain and the admin login must be in your name.
Website design cost in Mumbai at a glance (2026)

I went through 16 price guides that Mumbai and Indian agencies published in 2025–26. They don't agree on much, but the ranges below are where most of them overlap. All prices are one-time, before GST. Typical build times are further down.

Why one website costs ₹10,000 and another ₹1 lakh
The price is mostly time, and these are the things that take time:
Template or custom design.

A premium WordPress theme costs ₹3,000–₹7,000. Below about ₹25,000, most sites are a theme with your logo, colours and photos swapped in. That's fine for a lot of businesses, as long as you know that's what you're buying.
Words.

Someone has to write every page so that customers understand it and Google can match it to searches. If you write it yourself, the site costs less. If the designer writes it, it costs more, and it's usually better.
Features.
Booking, online ordering, payments, a product catalogue, or pages in Hindi, Marathi or Gujarati as well as English each add work.
Products.
An online store with 30 products and one with 300 are different projects, mainly because of photos, descriptions and filters.
Who builds it.
Freelancer projects mostly run ₹10,000–₹80,000. Agency projects mostly run ₹50,000–₹3 lakh, because you're also paying for a team and an office.
Deadline.
One guide says rush projects can cost 30–50% more. Planning a month ahead saves real money.

GST on a website: 18%, but not always
Agencies add 18%.
Website design is taxed at 18% GST. A registered agency adds it to your bill, so a ₹40,000 quote becomes ₹47,200.

6 red flags before you pay anyone
The domain is in their name or email.

Indian legal-advice sites are full of owners asking how to get their domain back from a developer who won't transfer it. Register the domain in your business's name, with your email, and keep the registrar login.
No admin login.
Owners describe fully paid sites where the developer then asked for more money to hand over the account. Get the website admin login and the hosting login at launch, in writing.

A maintenance contract should list exactly what's included (updates, backups, small edits) and end when you choose.

Ask what hosting and the domain will cost in year two, and which company hosts the site, so you can check the host's renewal price yourself.
A template sold as "custom design".
At ₹10,000 it's almost always a theme, which is fine if they say so. Ask for the theme's name.
No written scope.
Pages, rounds of changes, who writes the text, timelines and what costs extra should all be on paper before you pay the advance.

Will I get the admin login and hosting login at launch?

Who writes the text and who supplies the photos?

Is the design custom or a theme, and if it's a theme, which one?
How long does a website take?

A landing page takes 3–7 days. A basic business site takes 1–4 weeks, a custom-designed one 3–8 weeks, and an online store 4–12 weeks depending on the number of products. In my experience, the biggest delay is almost never the build. It's waiting for the photos, the prices and the text. Have those ready and any honest designer can move faster.

Why one website costs ₹10,000 and another ₹1 lakh

The price is mostly time, and these are the things that take time:

  1. The domain is in their name or email. Indian legal-advice sites are full of owners asking how to get their domain back from a developer who won't transfer it. Register the domain in your business's name, with your email, and keep the registrar login.

  2. No admin login. Owners describe fully paid sites where the developer then asked for more money to hand over the account. Get the website admin login and the hosting login at launch, in writing.

  3. A yearly "maintenance" fee you never agreed to. A maintenance contract should list exactly what's included (updates, backups, small edits) and end when you choose.

  4. No year-two price. Ask what hosting and the domain will cost in year two, and which company hosts the site, so you can check the host's renewal price yourself.

  2. Whose name and email will the domain be registered in?

  6. How many rounds of changes are included?

  7. What's covered after launch, for how long, and what do edits cost after that?

  8. Is the design custom or a theme, and if it's a theme, which one?

How long does a website take?

A landing page takes 3–7 days. A basic business site takes 1–4 weeks, a custom-designed one 3–8 weeks, and an online store 4–12 weeks depending on the number of products. In my experience, the biggest delay is almost never the build. It's waiting for the photos, the prices and the text. Have those ready and any honest designer can move faster.

faq.q: What is Ask Maps in Google Maps?

faq.q: Is Ask Maps available in India and in Hindi?
faq.a: Yes. Google launched Ask Maps in India on 12 March 2026 in English, on Android and iPhone, and added Hindi on 6 August 2026.

faq.q: How do I use Ask Maps?

content.text: Your customers can now ask Google Maps a full question, the way they'd ask a friend, and get an answer written by Google's Gemini AI. In Hindi too. What you can do is make sure everything Google knows about you is complete and correct: your Business Profile details, attributes, services, photos and reviews, and a website that says the same things. Then ask Ask Maps about your own area once a month and fix what's wrong.

posts.seo_description: Is WhatsApp Business free? App vs API costs in India, per-message rates, the 1 October 2026 changes and the 31 December INR billing deadline.

faq.q: Is WhatsApp Business free in India?
faq.a: The WhatsApp Business app is free to use: chatting, the catalogue, labels and quick replies cost nothing. Broadcasts to people who haven’t saved your number, Meta Verified and some extras are paid. The WhatsApp Business Platform (API) is paid per message delivered.

faq.q: What are WhatsApp API charges per message in India?
faq.a: Meta’s list prices in India, before tax, are about ₹0.8631 for a marketing message and ₹0.115 for a utility or authentication message. Replies inside a customer’s 24-hour window are free for the first 1,000 per number each month, then ₹0.115 each. Providers usually charge more per message, plus a monthly fee.

faq.q: What changed on WhatsApp on 1 October 2026?
faq.a: On the API, replies to customers are now free only for the first 1,000 per business number each month, utility templates sent inside the 24-hour window are now charged, and a payment method is required. The free WhatsApp Business app has no per-message charge.

faq.q: Do I need to switch my WhatsApp billing to INR?
faq.a: Meta requires India-billed solution providers and directly integrated API businesses to move to rupee billing by 31 December 2026, or their messages stop from 1 January 2027. If you use the API through a provider, ask them to confirm. App users don’t need to do anything.

faq.q: Are messages customers send me on WhatsApp charged?
faq.a: No. Meta charges businesses only for messages they send. Messages customers send you are free on both the app and the API.

content.text: "Kya WhatsApp Business free hai?" It's one of the questions shop owners ask me most, and in October it got harder to answer. On 1 October 2026 Meta changed what it charges on the WhatsApp Business Platform, and some news reports made it sound as if every WhatsApp business message is now paid. It isn't.
The confusion comes from two different products that share one name: the free WhatsApp Business
app

The short version:

the WhatsApp Business app is still free to use, though bulk broadcasts and some extras now cost money. The API charges per message delivered: about 86 paise for a marketing message in India and 11.5 paise for a utility message. Since 1 October 2026, API replies to customers are free only for the first 1,000 per number each month. Meta also requires India-billed API accounts to move to rupee billing by 31 December 2026. If you use the API through a provider, ask them to confirm they've done it.
The WhatsApp Business app vs the API

Most of the confusion goes away once you know which one you have. If you installed WhatsApp Business from the Play Store and chat from your phone, you're on the app. If a provider such as Interakt, AiSensy or Wati set up automated messages for you, you're on the API.

posts.content_html:
"Kya WhatsApp Business free hai?" It's one of the questions shop owners ask me most, and in October it got harder to answer. On 1 October 2026 Meta changed what it charges on the WhatsApp Business Platform, and some news reports made it sound as if every WhatsApp business message is now paid. It isn't.

The confusion comes from two different products that share one name: the free WhatsApp Business app on your phone, and the paid WhatsApp Business Platform, usually called the API, which businesses use for automation and bulk messages. This guide covers what each one costs in India today, what changed on 1 October, the 31 December billing deadline, and how to keep your bill small.

The short version: the WhatsApp Business app is still free to use, though bulk broadcasts and some extras now cost money. The API charges per message delivered: about 86 paise for a marketing message in India and 11.5 paise for a utility message. Since 1 October 2026, API replies to customers are free only for the first 1,000 per number each month. Meta also requires India-billed API accounts to move to rupee billing by 31 December 2026. If you use the API through a provider, ask them to confirm they've done it.

The WhatsApp Business app vs the API

Most of the confusion goes away once you know which one you have. If you installed WhatsApp Business from the Play Store and chat from your phone, you're on the app. If a provider such as Interakt, AiSensy or Wati set up automated messages for you, you're on the API.

What's still free on the WhatsApp Business app

Meta says it plainly on its own page: "The WhatsApp Business app stays free." Chatting with customers, the catalogue, labels, quick replies and greeting and away messages all cost nothing.

What costs money in the app:

  • Broadcasting beyond saved contacts. Old-style broadcast lists are free, but they reach only contacts who have saved your number, up to 256 per list. The newer business broadcasts tool (Tools, then Business broadcasts) can message customers who haven't saved your number, but beyond a free allowance it is paid. Meta started charging for this kind of message in India in September 2024. Check the current allowance and price in your app, because Meta changes them.

  • Meta Verified and Meta One. The verified badge and extra features are a monthly subscription. Meta Verified launched in India from ₹639 a month in 2024, and Meta is now bringing it into Meta One, a new subscription.

  • Business AI, past a point. The AI that answers customers for you is free "up to an included allowance", Meta says. It hasn't published how big that allowance is.

What changed on 1 October 2026 (API only)

Meta's developer pricing docs list the changes. They apply to the API, not the app:

  1. Replies are no longer unlimited and free. Each business phone number gets 1,000 free service messages (your normal replies inside a customer's 24-hour window) a month. Each one after that is charged. The free 1,000 don't roll over.

  2. Utility templates are charged even inside the 24-hour window. Order confirmations and reminders sent as templates were free inside the window from July 2025. Now they're charged.

  3. A payment method is needed. Without one, replies beyond the free 1,000 stop being delivered.

  4. Click-to-WhatsApp ads got more generous. If a customer messages you from one of these ads and you reply within 24 hours, Meta's docs say all your messages to them are free for a window of "up to 7 days". Many older pages still say 72 hours.

India's per-message rates did not change on 1 October. India's marketing rate last went up on 1 January 2026.

What a small shop really pays: an example

Take Meher Boutique in Ghatkopar, an invented example. In a busy month it sends 2,000 marketing messages to customers who opted in, 500 order updates, and 1,400 replies to customer questions.

  • Direct at Meta's list prices: 2,000 marketing messages at ₹0.8631 is ₹1,726. 500 utility messages at ₹0.115 is ₹57.50. Of the 1,400 replies, 1,000 are free and the other 400 cost ₹46. That's about ₹1,830 a month before GST.

  • Through a provider: at AiSensy's listed prices, the same messages cost about ₹2,310, plus its ₹1,500 starter plan. That's about ₹3,810 a month before GST.

The lesson: marketing messages are more than 90% of the bill. Replies and order updates barely register. To cut the bill, send fewer and better offers, not fewer replies.

The 31 December rupee billing deadline: who has to act?

Meta's docs say that "Solution Providers and directly-integrated businesses whose Sold-To country is India" must move their WhatsApp billing to rupees by 31 December 2026. From 1 January 2027, Meta "will no longer deliver the messages" of accounts that haven't moved.

  • On the free app? Nothing to do.

  • On the API through a provider? Your provider is usually the account holder, so it's their job. Ask them to confirm in writing that your account bills in INR.

  • Connected to the API directly and paying in dollars? You have to move it yourself in Meta's Billing Hub before 31 December.

Rules that can get your number limited

  • Messaging limits. A new business account can start conversations with 250 unique customers in a rolling 24 hours. The next level is 2,000, which you reach by verifying your business or by sending good-quality messages.

  • Opt-in. Meta requires customers to have clearly opted in to hear from your business. Buying number lists breaks this.

  • Quality. Templates that customers block or ignore get a lower rating and can be paused.

  • Per-customer limits. WhatsApp may limit how many marketing messages a customer gets from all businesses, based on how they engage. If yours are blocked, Meta advises waiting at least 24 hours before trying again.

6 ways to keep your WhatsApp bill down

  1. Send offers to the right people only. Use labels such as "Bridal", "Regular" or "Wholesale" and message each group about what they actually buy, such as bridal offers timed to the wedding season dates. Fewer messages, better results.

  2. Reply with normal messages, not templates. Inside the 24-hour window, a normal reply is free up to 1,000 a month. A utility template now costs money.

  3. Let customers message first. A "WhatsApp us" button on your Instagram profile and website brings customers in, and messages customers send you are never charged.

  4. Use click-to-WhatsApp ads for promotions. Reply within 24 hours and your messages to those customers are free for up to 7 days, per Meta's docs.

  5. Compare providers properly. Add their monthly plan to their per-message markup on your real volumes, not on their example.

  6. Stay on the app if it's enough. One phone, a few hundred regular customers and no automation? The free app and broadcast lists may be all you need.
